chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Nasr, from Abd al-Karim, from Abi Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
"The curse (l'an) does not take effect until the man has intercourse with his wife."

key_terms.اللَّعْنُ: The legal curse (l'an), a specific judicial procedure in Shia and Sunni fiqh where husband and wife mutually curse each other to prove or disprove adultery charges.
key_terms.بِأَهْلِهِ: With his wife (literally: with his 'household' or 'wife').
key_terms.حَتَّى: Until, indicating a condition that must be met for the preceding statement to become valid.
key_terms.يَدْخُلَ: To enter, specifically referring to sexual intercourse or consummation of marriage.

ai.seo_question: When does the Islamic legal procedure of l'an (mutual cursing) take effect?
ai.summary: In Shia jurisprudence, this hadith clarifies that the 'l'an' procedure is contingent upon actual marital intimacy, distinguishing it from cases where the couple has not yet consummated the union. This condition ensures that the legal presumption of paternity, which the curse seeks to refute, is firmly established through physical connection before the severe penalty of mutual imprecation is enacted.
